name: Lwel
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-017: create [lvl] Lwel (adopted 2023-01-20). 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; gives lexical-similarity figures (Nzadi 64%, Ding 59%) and lists the sources: Khang Levy 1979, Koni Muluwa & Bostoen 2015, Maselli et al. 2021, Pacchiarotti et al. 2019.

sources.citation: Maselli, Lorenzo, Sara Pacchiarotti & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Labial-velar stops outside the Macro-Sudan Belt: New evidence from Lwel (West-Coastal Bantu, B862). Africana Linguistica 27: 141-164. DOI 10.2143/AL.27.0.3290074 (accepted manuscript, 22 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2 reproduces the Lwel consonant inventory from Khang Levy 1979: 4 and gives phonetic evidence for /kp/ (and doubtful /gb/) from one Sedzo speaker recorded in Idiofa in 2019; forms carry H/L tone marks ('we added the notation of low tones'), but stress, accent, prominence and syllable structure are never mentioned. States: 'The dissertations by Khang Levy (1977, 1979) are the only descriptive studies of Lwel available to us.'

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Final vowel loss in Lower Kasai Bantu (DRC) as a contact-induced change. Journal of Language Contact 14: 437-475. DOI 10.1163/19552629-14020007 (published version, open access)
sources.note: Comparative historical phonology; Lwel B862 data come from Khang Levy 1979 and Koni Muluwa & Bostoen 2015 (p. 441). No mention of stress, accent or penultimate prominence for any language; states only that final vowel loss 'is not phonologically and/or prosodically determined or constrained' (p. 445), and that HL roots surface as HL or Falling on a lengthened vowel (fn. p. 447). Silent on Lwel stress.

sources.citation: Maselli, Pacchiarotti & Bostoen 2019 Lwel recordings (BantuFirst fieldwork, Idiofa), OSF project wbaq5
sources.note: Primary audio (c. 2 h elicited words) from the one Sedzo speaker; would allow a first-hand check of prominence/penultimate lengthening if no written statement surfaces.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: Identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 155-229. DOI 10.2143/AL.25.0.3287234 (accepted manuscript, 75 pp; text partly font-garbled)
sources.note: Classification and identification paper; distinguishes East Lwel (Sedzo, Khang Levy 1979) from an undocumented West Lwel (Mateko); Lwel lexical data from Khang Levy 1979. No stress content (a full-text search for stress/accent/penult: none).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference list for lwel1234 (16 records: Khang Levy 1979/1986/1987, Maselli et al. 2021, Maselli 2024, Koni Muluwa & Bostoen 2015, Pacchiarotti et al. 2019, Bostoen & Koni Muluwa 2014 Umlaut, Maes 1934 wordlist, Kalunga 1999, Bastin et al. 1999, Grollemund et al. 2015, Vansina 1966, Maes & Boone 1935, Kadima et al. 2008, ISO 2022-017); Maho 2009 NUGL entry 'B862 Lwel, Kelwer'
sources.note: Bibliographic only. No phonology-typed reference exists for Lwel in Glottolog; the only 'grammar sketch' is Khang Levy 1979.

sources.citation: Khang Levy, Nyi-m'shum. 1979. Eléments de grammaire morphologique de la langue lwel. Lubumbashi: UNAZA, mémoire de licence. 174 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Glottolog's sole descriptive reference; ch. 1 (pp. 1-4+) gives the phoneme inventory and presumably tone; may carry a prosody note. Held by BantUGent group (Bostoen/Pacchiarotti) and probably RMCA Tervuren library; not online.

sources.citation: Maselli, Lorenzo. 2024. Documenting the sounds of the West-Coastal Bantu languages of the Lower Kasai region (DR Congo): An integrated phonetic and diachronic-phonological approach. Ghent University PhD. 399 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern instrumental phonetic documentation of Lwel (Sedzo variety) among six languages; would supersede Khang Levy on segmental and likely on prosodic matters.
